claim.why_it_matters: The figure is titled 'Banking hierarchy' and its entire content is the inheritance relation; the two upward arrows are the only thing in the figure that says CheckingAccount and SavingAccount are subclasses of Account. Rendered as two unconnected tables, the markdown shows three peer classes and the hierarchy is gone, which is exactly what the surrounding text ('each instance of CheckingAccount ... methods deposit, withdraw, and balance inherited from Account') depends on the figure to illustrate. Note that Figure D.4 one page earlier DID keep its arrows (▲), so this is an isolated loss, not a house style.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED against both sources at 300 dpi. (1) PDF: I cropped and upscaled the connector band of E:/Temp/specrecon/v1143/spec_p1143.png (region x 550-2050, y 2150-2560) and read the glyphs directly. There are unambiguously TWO vertical solid rules, one rising from the centre of the top edge of the 'CheckingAccount' box and one from the centre of the top edge of the 'SavingAccount' box, each terminating in a SOLID FILLED triangular arrowhead whose tip touches the bottom edge of the 'Account' box. I also cropped the Account box (y 1750-2300) and confirmed the three compartments ('Account' / 'account-number, balance, date-opened' / 'deposit, withdraw, balance') and the two side labels 'Data items' and 'Methods', each drawn as a horizontal rule ending in a solid filled arrowhead aimed at the second and third compartments respectively. The claim's description of the PDF is accurate in every particular. (2) Markdown: I read the claimed text out of the canonical file, not just the work-unit extract - specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 45980-45991 contain exactly the two pipe tables quoted in the claim, verbatim. There is no connector, no arrow glyph, no line, no
note, and no prose caption anywhere in the figure block that states the inheritance edges. So the claim misquotes neither source. (3) Adversarial checks I ran and that FAILED to refute: the 'missing' content is not reflowed onto an adjacent line - the paragraph immediately following the figure block is the 'In the example shown...' body text, and the paragraph immediately preceding is the 'A bank will have different kinds of accounts...' body text; nothing between them carries the edges. The loss is not page-break furniture - the whole figure sits on one page in the PDF. It is not mere formatting: rendering a box as a table row is a legitimate transcription convention and the compartment CONTENTS all survive intact (including ISO's own 'SavingAccount' vs prose 'SavingsAccount' inconsistency, which is faithfully carried over), so the tables-instead-of-boxes choice is NOT the defect - the defect is the two directed edges, which are semantic content in a UML-style class diagram and whose DIRECTION (subclass to superclass) is what encodes the relation. (4) The claim's cross-reference also checks out: Figure D.4, specs/ISO_COBOL.md around line 45940, is transcribed as a fenced ASCII-art block using box-drawing characters and two '▲' glyphs to carry the Person/Employee/Manager hierarchy, so D.5 losing its connectors is inconsistent with the immediately preceding figure in the same subclause (D.19.5.1) rather than a uniform house style.
verdict.corrected_description: The finding is real as described, with one correction to its framing and severity. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOST, precisely: only the two inheritance connectors. Everything else in Figure D.5 survives the transcription - all three boxes, all three compartments of each box, every data item and method name, and both side labels (the drawn arrows on 'Data items' and 'Methods' are rendered as '→', which is faithful). So the defect is not 'the figure was mangled into tables'; it is that the two solid lines with filled arrowheads running from the top edge of CheckingAccount and from the top edge of SavingAccount up to the bottom edge of Account are absent, leaving the markdown showing three peer classes with no stated relation. CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM'S FRAMING: the claim overstates the consequence when it says 'the hierarchy is gone'. It is gone FROM THE FIGURE, but not from the page - the markdown prose on both sides of the figure states the relation explicitly and survives intact ('use inheritance to define the checking account and the savings account subclasses' before it; 'the methods deposit, withdraw, and balance inherited from Account' after it). CORRECTION TO SEVERITY: Annex D is headed '(informative)' at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 41494, and Figure D.5 is a worked illustration inside D.19.5.1 Inheritance. No normative rule, general format, or compiler behaviour depends on this figure, so 'structural' overstates the impact for implementation purposes - this is a figure-fidelity defect in informative material, best classified cosmetic-to-minor. RECOMMENDED FIX (matching the house style already used for D.4 twelve lines earlier): replace the two pipe tables with a single fenced ASCII-art block drawing the Account box above the two subclass boxes with '▲'-headed risers from each subclass to Account, or, if the tables are retained, add a '> **Figure notes (Figure D.5 — Banking hierarchy).**' line stating that solid lines with arrowheads run from the top of CheckingAccount and SavingAccount to the bottom of Account, denoting that both are subclasses of Account.
